r: **Sufism is closest to Bhakti (devotion)** – rather than karma, kalpa or gyana
**Verses in the languages of their followers**
Rejecting priests, idol worship and women in temples

0.x: Bhakti stressed devotion over Vedic ritual; Sufism valued inner experience over formal law. Kabir and Nanak criticised the orthodoxy of **both Hinduism and Islam**; the meeting of the two produced a **composite Indo-Islamic culture**.

r: Chishti (and Suhrawardi) assemblies; **Amir Khusrau** introduced the **Qaul**; Naqshbandis opposed sama; early Chishtis were fond of sama
**Many Sanskrit music works were translated into Persian** through rulers' interest: Ghunyat-ul-Munya (**1375**), **Lahjat-i-Sikandar Shahi** (Sikandar Lodi)
Shaped largely by **Arabo-Persian** music brought by Muslim rulers and Sufis
Stayed tied to temple Bhakti; Telugu composers
Practised by the **Nathpanthis**; its technique was **adopted by the Sufis**

2.x: **13th-century** Sufis met the Kanphata yogis; the **Amritakund** (Hath-yoga text) went into Arabic and Persian; breath control was used in all orders except the **Naqshbandi**.

**Nizamuddin Auliya** was struck by the yogic division of the body into **Siva** (head to navel) and **Sakti** (below); **Hamiduddin Nagori** equated **Alakh Niranjan** with **Khuda** in Hindi verse. The interaction went beyond temple ritual.

r: First medieval reformer to denounce caste outright (disciples Kabir, Raidas, Sena, Dhanna)
Against caste; widow remarriage, gender equality
Sayyid reformer among the Madigas of **Vinukonda**

3.x: **Women saints:** Mirabai, Andal, **Lal Ded (Lalla)**, Janabai, Bahinabai, **Molla** (Molla Ramayanam); Dhanna was a man.

r: **Guru Ghasidas** (c. 1820s); an earlier Satnami sect began at Narnaul under Birbhan (1657)
Dadu, **Rajasthan**; Sant tradition with Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas
**Sheikh Nuruddin (Nund Rishi)**, **Kashmir**; inspired by Lal Ded; universal love, service to all castes, **vegetarianism**
Carried the syncretic line; Sirhindi opposed it
Kabir, Tulsidas, Surdas; Amir Khusrau (Urdu / Hindavi)
Vemana (satire on birth-based inequality), Veerabrahmam (**Kalagnanam**), Potana

4.x: Both movements preached in the **language of the masses** and enriched Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Punjabi and other regional languages.

r: **Caste persisted**; Srivaishnavism and Veerashaivism opposed caste but could not eradicate it
The traditions **hardened into separate sects and panths**
Failed to reform Hinduism and unite Hindus and Muslims, though they changed society deeply
